relationship: Packetising a message and sending it over an editable topology connects headers, payloads, routes and delivery checks.

learnerLoop.action: Enter a message, set packet options, create packets and send them.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The message is split into queued packets which travel over the chosen topology.
learnerLoop.evidence: Packet, route and arrival metrics plus the send queue show the transfer.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Adjust payload, checks or topology and compare the delivery result.

invariants: Packets shown in the queue derive from the current message and payload setting.
Delivery behaviour uses the displayed topology and selected processing options.
safeAdaptations: Change messages, network stories or constraints while preserving packet creation and route-based evidence.
nonGoals: Sending data over a real network.

task.description: Deliver a complete message; preparation status remains beside the send queue.
task.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

model.description: Restored sender / router-network / receiver columns; sender queue remains with Device A.
model.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

controls.description: Prepare/send message and select optional headers, checksum, expanded checks or first-trip corruption.
controls.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

evidence.description: Arrival inspection, rejection/retry, ordering buffer and reconstructed message.
evidence.visibility: Present throughout; content follows the current simulation state.

payload.domain: At most 72 characters; payload sizes 4, 6 or 8.
payload.output: Packet cards, sequence counts and reconstruction.

delivery.description: Packet attempts, arrival order and acceptance.
delivery.domain: Per-packet sequence, route, first arrival and retry counts.
delivery.source: Route scheduling and optional checksum corruption.
delivery.output: Arrival buffer, reconstructed text and delivery metrics.

graph.domain: Editable graph with five routers initially.

modes.processing: Headers and checksum optional; expanded checks adds detail. Corruption requires checksum and damages one packet on its first trip.
modes.speed: Slow, Normal and Fast change animation timing.

dependencies: Create packets before sending changed message/payload settings.
Checksum rejection causes NAK and retransmission; reassembly follows sequence rather than arrival order.
implementation.completion: Transmission completes when packet processing finishes; reconstructed message and accepted counts show whether delivery succeeded.
limitations: Routing and scheduling are illustrative and include runtime randomness.
Packet identity colours distinguish packets and are not correctness states.
